new_task_1.title: Load Emscripten worker source during fetcher startup
new_task_1.description: The Emscripten fetch transport no longer reads emscripten_fetch_worker.js into a module-level constant as soon as the module is evaluated. The worker script is read from package resources when a _StreamingFetcher is initialized, preserving streaming worker setup while avoiding worker-source loading in environments or code paths that do not create a streaming fetcher.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that urllib3's Emscripten fetch module loads the streaming worker JavaScript source as part of _StreamingFetcher initialization rather than as an unconditional module-level side effect.

expectation.grounded: urllib3.contrib.emscripten.fetch should not define or populate a module-level _STREAMING_WORKER_CODE value by reading emscripten_fetch_worker.js during module evaluation. When _StreamingFetcher is constructed, it should read emscripten_fetch_worker.js from the package resources using UTF-8 text decoding and pass that source into the JavaScript Blob used for worker startup.
expectation.conceptual: Users and environments that import the Emscripten fetch module without constructing the streaming fetcher should avoid unnecessary worker-script resource I/O, while streaming-worker-capable environments should still initialize the same worker code when the fetcher is created.

constraints.grounded: Do not change the package resource path, text encoding, JavaScript Blob construction, Blob content type, streaming fetcher state initialization, or worker behavior once _StreamingFetcher is instantiated. Do not require Emscripten fetch environments that never construct _StreamingFetcher to load the streaming worker source during module evaluation.
constraints.conceptual: The change should affect only when the streaming worker source is loaded, not what worker code is loaded or how streaming fetch behaves after initialization.

behavior: The Emscripten fetch module does not create or populate a module-level _STREAMING_WORKER_CODE value during module evaluation.
Constructing _StreamingFetcher reads emscripten_fetch_worker.js from the current package resources.
The worker source read during _StreamingFetcher initialization is supplied to js.Blob through to_js with create_pyproxies disabled.
The streaming worker Blob continues to use the application/javascript content type.
Failures related to reading the streaming worker source occur when streaming fetcher initialization is attempted rather than before the module has decided whether to create a streaming fetcher.
acceptance_criteria: Given an Emscripten environment that imports urllib3.contrib.emscripten.fetch but does not construct _StreamingFetcher, when the module import completes, then emscripten_fetch_worker.js should not have been read solely as an unconditional module-level side effect.
Given _StreamingFetcher is constructed, when it initializes its worker, then it should read emscripten_fetch_worker.js from the package resources with UTF-8 decoding.
Given _StreamingFetcher is constructed, when the worker Blob is created, then the Blob should receive the loaded worker source and retain the application/javascript content type.
Given normal streaming fetch behavior after _StreamingFetcher initialization, requests should continue to use the same packaged worker script behavior as before the load-timing change.

Given the worker resource is missing or unreadable, when no streaming fetcher is constructed, then importing the fetch module should not fail solely because that streaming worker resource cannot be read.
